title: Finite-limit preservation by affine associated sheafification
statement: For every commutative ring A, the associated sheaf functor from A-modules to modules on Spec(A) [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] preserves all finite limits. There are no nonzero-ring or finiteness hypotheses on the modules.

proof.text: For each morphism f of A-modules, its sheafified kernel is quasi-coherent. Its affine counit is therefore invertible. Lift the kernel inclusion and its zero-composite identity through the fully faithful tilde functor. The image fork is isomorphic to the sheaf kernel fork, hence a limit. Reflect the limit using full faithfulness, proving that tilde preserves this kernel.

The tilde adjunction makes tilde a left adjoint; preservation of binary biproducts gives additivity. Apply Functor.preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesKernels using the kernel preservation for every morphism.

proof_origin.note: Repair: generalize the inaccessible private kernel-preservation helper to a shared public finite-limit theorem, used by both Koszul comparison modules.
